That the petitioner purchased the tenanted premises by virtue of registered sale deed dated 04.08.2006 executed by Smt. Renu Jain, Sh.
Rajesh Jain, Sh. Rakesh Kumar and Sh. Vimal Jain in favour of petitioner.

That one Lt. Sh. Hari Chand was a tenant in the tenanted premises prior to purchase of the tenanted premises by the petitioner and after the death of Sh. Hari Chand, the tenancy was inherited by only one of his legal heirs / son i.e. Sh. Veer Singh Thakur and he had lastly paid rent of Rs.400/- in respect of tenanted premises on 31.08.2009.
Thus, there is no relationship of landlord and tenant between the petitioner and the other legal heirs of Lt. Sh. Hari Chand.
That the respondent no.4 (one of the sons of Lt. Sh. Hari Chand) never remained in use and occupation of the tenanted premises, however, he wanted to grab the same in one way or the other.

That Sh. Veer Singh expired leaving behind his legal heirs i.e. Smt. Anita (wife), Sh. Shelly (son) and Ms. Pooja (daughter) i.e. respondent no.1,
respondent no.2 and respondent no.3 respectively but the tenanted premises was illegally sublet by the original tenant to respondent no.5, signed by PRAGATI PRAGATI Date:

3) Summons of the present petition were served upon the respondents no.4 and 5 on 10.03.2022 and written statement was filed on behalf of respondent no.4.

Summons were served upon the respondents no.1 to 3 by way of publication on 07.10.2022,
however, none had appeared on behalf of the respondents no.1 to 3 and 5 before the court therefore, vide order dated 13.10.2022 and 07.12.2022, respectively, the respondents no. 1 to 3 and respondent no.5 respectively were proceeded against ex-parte.

That the petitioner has filed forged and fabricated rent receipts showing the rent of Rs.400/- p.m.
That respondent no.4 is running his shop in the tenanted premises and has not sublet the same to anyone.

That the respondent no.4 had filed DR petition bearing no.58/2016 before the court for deposition of rent and therein the petitioner had filed his objections and the same were dismissed and the petitioner was directed to provide his account details to the respondent no.4 so that the rent may be deposited but the petitioner did not provide the account details and has been receiving the rent without issuing rent receipt.

14)Final arguments advanced by Ld. Counsel for petitioner and Ld. Counsel for the LRs of respondent No.4 heard.
Case file perused carefully.

15) Having heard the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner and having thoroughly perused the entire record of the case, it is to be considered by this Court whether the respondent is liable to be evicted from the tenanted premises/shop on the grounds under Section 14 (1) (b) of the DRC Act.

16) Section 14 (1) (b) of DRC Act as read as follows:- The Protection of tenant against eviction.-(1) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any other law or contract, no order or decree for the recovery of possession of any premises shall be made by any court or Controller in favour of the landlord against a tenant:

Provided that the Controller may, on an application made to him in the prescribed manner,
make an order for the recovery of possession of the premises on one or more of the following Digitally signed by PRAGATI PRAGATI Date:
2026.02.11 18:30:44 +0530 grounds only, namely:-(b) that the tenant has, on or after the 9th day of June, 1952, sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord.
17) Hence, following essentials will be examined in the present case- i. Relationship of landlord and tenant exist between the parties.

ii. Tenant has sublet, assigned,
parted with the possession of whole or any part of the tenanted premises.
iii. No written consent of the petitioner was obtained prior to the subletting.
Analysis/reasoning 18)
In the present petition, the fact that the petitioner is the owner as well as the landlord qua the tenanted premises is an admitted fact and thus, the same is not in dispute.
